sample_size.second_extractor_value: 500 community water systems: 321 government-owned, 121 cooperative, and 58 investor-owned; systems were located in 321 counties

study_design.second_extractor_value: Cross-sectional observational analysis using OLS regressions for the 500 largest US community water systems, principally using 2015 water-price and system data

effect_estimate.second_extractor_value: Private ownership was associated with a $144.04 higher annual bill (standardized coefficient 0.35, p<0.01) and a 1.55-percentage-point higher water-income burden for lowest-quintile households (standardized coefficient 0.26, p<0.01). Favorable private regulation in New Jersey and Pennsylvania was associated with an $88.64 higher annual bill (p<0.01).

risk_of_bias_tool.second_extractor_value: JBI Analytical Cross Sectional Studies checklist is appropriate

mechanism_certainty.comment: The observational regressions document associations but do not directly observe the causal mechanism.

outcome_flags.second_extractor_value: affordability only; measured outcomes were annual water bill and the percentage of lowest-quintile household income spent on water
outcome_flags.comment: Water access and service continuity/disconnection were discussed but not measured as study outcomes.

mechanism_flags.second_extractor_value: fees; property/ownership; regulatory oversight may broadly support enforcement and administrative_review
mechanism_flags.comment: The remaining flags were contextual mentions or unsupported as mechanisms examined by the study.
